dataset: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List -- Advanced XML
description: US Treasury OFAC's own sanctions list distribution, including typed 'Digital Currency Address - <ASSET>' identifiers attached to designated parties. The only source in this project where a government document directly names both an on-chain address and the legal entity/program that address was designated under, in one record.
license_note: A work of the US federal government; not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. Sec. 105). Freely redistributable, same posture as any other US Treasury public sanctions publication.

schema_notes.format: One <DistinctParty FixedRef=...> per designated party. Identity/Alias/DocumentedName supplies the legal name and aliases; zero or more <Feature FeatureTypeID=...> elements carry a typed identifier -- this adapter reads only the FeatureTypes named 'Digital Currency Address - XBT/ETH/TRX', the three chains CyberTrace has an entity type for. FeatureType IDs are read from the file's own <ReferenceValueSets> rather than hardcoded, since OFAC has changed them across schema revisions.
schema_notes.not_parsed: Per-entity designation date, sanctions program code, jurisdiction, and remarks text are NOT extracted by this adapter -- they live in a separate <SanctionsEntry> section cross-referenced by profile ID, and in free-text Remarks that are not reliably structured. Provenance here is the SDN publication date (this manifest's publication_date) plus the OFAC profile ID (FixedRef), which is sufficient to cite and re-verify a specific entry -- not a substitute for reading the underlying designation action when jurisdiction/program detail matters.
schema_notes.currencies_indexed: Only BTC (OFAC code XBT), ETH, and TRX -- same restriction as integrations/exchange_tags.py. OFAC's schema carries 20 digital-asset types total (ARB, BNB, BSC, BSV, DASH, DOGE, ETC, LTC, SOL, USDC, USDT, XMR, XRP, XVG, ZEC, ...); rows for unsupported chains are read and dropped at index-build time.

safety_boundary: An OFAC entry here is a REGULATORY_ATTESTED government designation of a specific address -- the strongest evidence class this project has, but still an assertion that a specific address is associated with a specific SDN-listed party, not proof that every address which later transacts with it shares that party's ownership or is itself sanctioned. It must never be written as an EXCHANGE_DEPOSIT or any other relationship automatically -- see cybertrace/integrations/ofac.py and correlate.py's REGULATORY_ATTESTED handling in _vasp_endpoints. Only evidence.label_exchange, on an analyst's own say-so, may write that edge. A subset of these designations (e.g. Hydra Market, a darknet marketplace; Blender.io, a mixing service) are not VASPs at all -- REGULATORY_ATTESTED names an OFAC-designated entity, not a VASP-ownership claim, and callers must render it that way rather than defaulting to 'VASP' wording.
